claims.statement: The separate admin listener starts only in OAuth pool mode with admin explicitly enabled; its address is configurable with a default of 0.0.0.0:9090, and a bind failure is logged without aborting the inference listener.

Kubernetes enables the admin listener on port 9090 with a dedicated ClusterIP service; Tailscale Ingress points to the inference service instead, the admin router adds no authentication check, and the account runbook uses kubectl port-forward for access.

The active authorization endpoint is https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize and the redirect URI is https://platform.claude.com/oauth/code/callback. The hosted callback displays code#state for manual submission to the admin API rather than calling it.

The authorization URL uses a public client ID, code=true, response_type=code, an S256 challenge and random state, and the subscription profile, inference, Claude Code session, and MCP scopes; it does not request Console API-key creation.

Admin init independently generates the verifier and opaque state from 32 random bytes each encoded as 43 unpadded base64url characters, returns the URL, account ID and state, and retains the verifier, ID and creation time under state in process memory.

Pending PKCE state has a ten-minute window with lazy cleanup at init; it is instance-local and lost on restart, so init and completion must reach the same process. The shipped deployment uses one replica.

Completion accepts code#state or a code with a separate state field; the suffix takes precedence and an optional account ID is only a match check against the saved ID. Missing or unknown state, an ID mismatch, or expired state returns 400.

Completion removes a matching PKCE entry before checking the optional ID and expiry, exchanging tokens or writing credentials. ID mismatch, expiry, exchange failure (502) and storage failure (500) after lookup leave no state to retry, requiring a new init.
The account ID is derived from Unix seconds at init, so two flows initialized in the same second can have different state values but write the same credential key on completion.

The auth crate posts to https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token for both exchange and refresh. Code exchange uses an authorization_code form grant with code, state, original verifier, public client ID and redirect URI.

Successful completion converts expires_in seconds to an absolute Unix millisecond expiry and writes the OAuth access and refresh credential under the saved account ID before setting that account available in the live pool and returning status added, without a restart.

The credential store serializes JSON writes via a mutex and same-directory temp-file rename, setting Unix permissions to 0600. A failed add write does not roll back the in-memory credential mutation, but the admin handler returns 500 and does not proceed to pool activation.

Enrollment modifies the credential store and live pool, not config; at startup saved credential IDs seed the pool when providers is empty, while a nonempty providers list overrides them. Kubernetes ships with providers empty and persists /data/credentials.json on a PVC.
The pool owns runtime status separately from persisted credentials and reads tokens from the shared credential store at selection time.

GET /admin/accounts returns only per-account pool rows with IDs, status and applicable cooldown seconds, while GET /admin/pool returns those same rows plus counts and aggregate health. Both omit tokens and /admin/pool returns HTTP 200 even when the pool is unhealthy.

DELETE removes account membership and status first, then removes the in-memory credential and persists if it existed; this is local removal rather than upstream revocation and deleting an absent ID also succeeds.

Credential persistence failure on DELETE logs a warning but still returns HTTP 200 with status removed. Old disk data can reload at startup, and a repeat DELETE alone will not rewrite it once the in-memory credential is absent.

Both inline and background refresh disable accounts on permanent credential rejection (invalid_grant or HTTP 401/403), but not on transient failures. Restarting with the same credential does not restore an expired grant.

PKCE enrollment gives the proxy a separate refresh-token lineage from a local Claude Code login; runbook evidence puts recent PKCE grant failures near 30 days, a planning estimate rather than a guaranteed vendor lifetime or a demonstrated longevity advantage.

The recovery runbook has operators port-forward, enroll a new grant via PKCE, confirm that account is available, remove the disabled entry by ID, and verify the /health body and a client request because runtime status and HTTP health codes alone do not validate inference.

Focused admin tests exercise URL/state shape, missing or unknown and expired state, consumption on ID mismatch, token-free listing and deletion behavior. Auth tests cover PKCE encoding, file reload, Unix permissions and concurrent writes, and token endpoint configuration and error classification, but do not substitute for a successful hosted consent and deployed client smoke check.
